polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. The Cambridge Materials Data Book, 2003 edition (R-CUED-MATERIALS-DATA-BOOK-2003), a teaching reference whose polymer data are Granta Design's, gives thermoplastic polyurethane (tpPU) 1.12-1.24 Mg/m³ (Section II.2, Density, PDF p. 12); the row's 1050-1300 is wider. No producer's sheet with a readable figure was registered for TPU.

Ketones such as acetone, methylethylketone (MEK) and cyclohexanone are partial solvents for thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers. Elastollan products are unsuitable for long-term use in these solvents. Methyl ethyl ketone: volume swelling 105 % / 110 % / 130 %, reduction of tensile strength 80 % / 80 % / 90 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); other short-chained aliphatic ketones such as acetone have a similar effect.
PDF p. 2 Solvents; PDF p. 7 table 16.4

Harder products swell less and resist better. A filament's base (ester or ether) is usually not published.

Aliphatic alcohols, such as ethanol and isopropanol, cause swelling of Elastollan products. This is combined with a loss of tensile strength. Lubricating oils and greases (IRM 901, 902, 903 test oils)
Immersion at room temperature; 3 weeks at 100 °C

No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. There is also no reduction in tensile strength after 3 weeks immersion at 100 °C. Elastollan is in principal resistant to lubricating oils and greases, however irreversible damage can be caused by included additives. Compatibility testing in each individual lubricant is to be recommended.
PDF p. 2 Lubricating oils and greases
Saturated hydrocarbons (diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether, kerosene)

Contact of Elastollan with saturated hydrocarbons such as diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether and kerosene results in a limited swelling. At room temperature, this swelling amounts to approx. 1-3 % and the resultant reduction in tensile strength is no more than 20 %. After evaporation and reversal of the swelling, the original mechanical properties are almost completely restored.

Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)

If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
